specName: React Router URL Routing + Spec Completion Status
title: rorca-frontend-routing
_notes: Replace panel-switching state with React Router. Every panel gets a bookmarkable URL. Also adds 'completed' spec status so finished runs show correctly in Archive. Sonnet-tier — straightforward refactor, no architectural decisions.
_relatesTo: rorca-ui-redesign (established the panel architecture), rorca-ui-redesign-p2 (polish layer). Independent of CIE/convention-agents — can run anytime.
_executionOrder: Can run immediately — no dependencies on pending specs. Should run BEFORE rorca-e2e-testing so Playwright tests can navigate via URLs instead of clicking sidebar items.

userStories.title: Install React Router and Create Route Table
userStories.description: Install react-router-dom. Create a route table that maps every PanelId to a URL path. Wrap the app in BrowserRouter. Replace the activePanel useState in App.tsx with a Router Outlet pattern. The route table should mirror the NAV_SECTIONS structure from Sidebar.tsx: /forge, /queue, /archive, /marketplace (Specs section), /pipeline, /worktrees, /compare (Pipeline section), /direction, /team-direction (Direction section), /usage, /costs, /models, /velocity, /completion, /roi, /finops, /health (Analytics section), /audit-log, /activity, /github, /workspace-settings, /settings (System section). Hub is the index route at /. All routes render inside the Shell layout (Sidebar + content area). Configure Vite's dev server with historyApiFallback so direct URL access and browser refresh work.
acceptanceCriteria: react-router-dom is in package.json dependencies
Every PanelId has a corresponding route path in the route table
App.tsx uses BrowserRouter and Outlet instead of activePanel state and conditional rendering
Navigating to localhost:5210/forge renders the Forge panel
Navigating to localhost:5210/ renders the Hub panel (index route)
Browser refresh on any route re-renders the correct panel (Vite historyApiFallback configured)
Unknown routes redirect to / (hub)
Shell layout (sidebar + content area) wraps all routes as a layout route

userStories.title: Migrate Sidebar and Programmatic Navigation
userStories.description: Replace all setActivePanel() calls with react-router-dom navigate() or <Link> components. Update Sidebar.tsx nav items to use <NavLink> with active state styling (the existing isActive logic maps to NavLink's isActive prop). Update Shell.tsx handleNavigate callback. Update CommandPalette navigation commands to use navigate(). Update any notification click handlers, toast action buttons, or other programmatic navigation that calls setActivePanel(). The active panel highlight in the sidebar should derive from the current route (useLocation) instead of comparing against activePanel state.
acceptanceCriteria: Sidebar nav items are <NavLink> components with correct 'to' paths
Active sidebar item highlight derives from current URL (useLocation or NavLink isActive)
CommandPalette 'Go to...' commands use navigate() instead of setActivePanel()
No remaining references to setActivePanel in the codebase (grep confirms zero matches)
Clicking sidebar items changes the URL in the browser address bar
Browser back/forward buttons navigate between previously visited panels

userStories.title: SlideOver Deep Linking via Nested Routes
userStories.description: Replace the hash-based SlideOver routing (#/run/:runId) with proper nested routes. Run View becomes /runs/:runId (not nested under /hub). Spec Review becomes /specs/:specId/review. Remove the hashchange event listener from App.tsx. The SlideOver opens when the nested route matches and closes when navigating back. navigateToRun() becomes navigate(`/runs/${runId}`). navigateBackFromRun() becomes navigate(-1) or navigate('/'). Update any links that construct #/run/N URLs to use /runs/N paths. SSE event handlers that auto-navigate to a run on pipeline start should use navigate().
acceptanceCriteria: localhost:5210/runs/42 opens the Run View SlideOver for run 42
localhost:5210/specs/my-spec/review opens the Spec Review SlideOver
No remaining hash-based routing (grep for '#/run' returns zero matches)
hashchange event listener removed from App.tsx
Browser back button closes SlideOver and returns to previous panel
Direct URL access to /runs/:runId works (shows SlideOver over Hub)
Pipeline start SSE events that auto-open run view use navigate()

userStories.title: Settings Sub-Routes and SPA Fallback
userStories.description: Settings panel has sub-tabs (Direction Stack, Models & Providers, Account, Billing, etc.) managed by SettingsSidebar. Convert these to nested routes under /settings/: /settings/direction, /settings/models, /settings/account, /settings/billing, etc. The SettingsSidebar tabs become <NavLink> components. Default /settings redirects to /settings/direction (or first tab). Also configure Express static serving (RORCA_SERVE_STATIC mode) with SPA fallback — all non-API routes should serve index.html so deep links work in production self-hosted mode. Verify the Vite proxy config doesn't interfere with client-side routing.
acceptanceCriteria: localhost:5210/settings/direction renders Settings panel with Direction Stack tab active
localhost:5210/settings/models renders Settings panel with Models & Providers tab active
SettingsSidebar tabs are <NavLink> components deriving active state from URL
/settings redirects to /settings/direction (default sub-route)
Express static serving (RORCA_SERVE_STATIC=1) serves index.html for all non-/api routes
Browser refresh on /settings/models re-renders the correct tab
activeSettingsTab state in App.tsx is removed — settings tab derived from route params

userStories.title: Spec Completion Status in Archive
userStories.description: Add a 'completed' status to the spec lifecycle. Currently specs stay 'approved' forever after pipeline runs finish. When a pipeline run finishes with status 'done' (all stories passed), update the spec's status to 'completed'. Add 'completed' to the SpecStatus type in ArchivePanel.tsx. Add 'Completed' to the status filter dropdown in Archive. Update the archive GET endpoint to return completed specs (query pipeline_runs for specs with status='done', join with spec metadata). Add a green 'COMPLETED' badge in the archive card (matching the existing APPROVED/PENDING/REJECTED badge pattern). The spec file stays in forge/specs/approved/ — the completion status is tracked in the database only (via spec_versions or a new completed_at column on pipeline_runs already tracking this). Do NOT move spec files to a new directory.
acceptanceCriteria: SpecStatus type includes 'completed' alongside pending/approved/rejected
Archive status filter dropdown shows 'Completed' option
Specs with at least one pipeline run where status='done' show as COMPLETED in archive
COMPLETED badge is green, visually distinct from APPROVED badge
Filtering by 'Completed' shows only specs with successful runs
Filtering by 'Approved' shows only specs that are approved but have NOT been run (or have no successful run)
spec_versions table CHECK constraint updated to include 'completed' (via pragma table_info pattern)
Pipeline completion handler (run_finished with status=done) updates spec status to completed
Spec files remain in forge/specs/approved/ — no filesystem move on completion
